items.title: CleanYourTV for LG webOS
items.text:
A fast home screen for rooted LG webOS TVs. It replaces LG's Home with a dock of four apps, a top shelf and an app grid, and adds Live TV from your own playlist, an Inputs list on the Input key, picture notifications from your network, optional on-device voice recognition, and an optional debloat of LG's ads and telemetry.

A fork

This is a fork of lasharor/cleanyourtv-WebOS, with a photo screensaver, a Glass theme and security hardening on top. About this fork says what it adds and gives the credit.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
• Launcher. A dock of four apps, a top shelf with the focused app's name and an ambient glow, an app grid sorted by how often you use each app, an Inputs picker, a Settings shortcut and a clock. More.
  • Live TV. Plays your M3U playlist with a channel list, a programme guide (XMLTV) and number entry. It does not use LG's tuner. More.
  • Input key. The remote's Input button opens an Inputs list over the running app. More.
  • Picture notifications. A card with a photo over whatever is on screen, triggered from your network, for example by Home Assistant. More.
  • Voice (optional). Speech recognition on the TV (Moonshine), with answers from Home Assistant's Assist, a language model through OpenRouter or your own server, shown as text. More.
  • Debloat. Stops LG's ad and telemetry services and blocks a few ad servers. More.
  • Manager app. Sets up, updates and removes everything from the TV. More.

LG's system files are not modified. The launcher takes over Home with a mount that exists only in RAM, so a reboot without the boot scripts brings LG's Home back. Everything we install is stored in /media/developer/cleanyourtv (plus two boot scripts and the key binds), and the uninstall removes it. The project has no server or account and collects no data; optional features contact the services you choose (update checks go to GitHub). See What it changes on the TV and Security.

items.title: Compatibility at a glance
items.text:
Needs An LG webOS TV that is rooted with the Homebrew Channel. Install from the Homebrew Channel, or with one command over SSH as root. webOS webOS 5 and newer (2020 models and later). webOS 4 and older have no systemd and an old Node.js; setup stops before it changes anything. Tested LG OLED65G26LA on webOS 25. Other TVs are reported in Tested TVs. Not needed A computer app, a server, a cloud account. The service runs on the TV.

This modifies a TV with root access

Read install.sh and the scripts it installs before you run them, and use the project at your own risk. The setup saves the original state, and a failed start restarts the TV with LG's Home, but nothing here is covered by a warranty.

items.title: Where to start
items.text:
1. Make sure the TV is rooted and has the Homebrew Channel (rootmy.tv).
  2. Follow Installing: add CleanYourTV's repository to the Homebrew Channel (or run one command from your computer), then Set up now in the app on the TV.
  3. Check the tested TVs and report yours if it is not listed.

Questions and ideas are welcome on the CleanYourTV Discord; bugs go in the issues.

items.text: CleanYourTV is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by LG Electronics. LG and webOS are trademarks of LG Electronics. Live TV plays only the playlists you add; the project provides no channels and no playlist.

items.title: Working on problems with an AI assistant
items.text: If something does not work on your TV, an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, a local model) can help you find out why, and, if you want, help you fix the bug in the code and send the fix. This page says what to give it and how to keep it safe. Nothing here is required: Share log and an issue work as before.

items.title: The ground rules
items.text:
• Read-only first. The assistant reads a report. It may run read-only commands on the TV. Anything that changes the TV (restart a service, edit a file, install, delete, reboot) is proposed first, you say yes, and it names the command that undoes it.
  • You decide what leaves your house. A report goes to whatever AI service you use. Addresses, MAC addresses, stream URLs and tokens are masked, but masking is best effort: read the file before you paste or upload it. A local model keeps it on your computer.
  • An assistant can be wrong. Do not run a command you do not understand. The way back is always the same: switch CleanYourTV as Home off in the manager app, or sh /media/developer/cleanyourtv/undo-home.sh, or start the TV in the Homebrew Channel's failsafe mode.

items.title: Part 1: find out what is wrong on your TV
items.text:
1. Collect a report. In the manager app Share log shows a QR code for a masked report, or from your computer:
git clone https://github.com/LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS && cd cleanyourtv-WebOS
sh tools/diagnose.sh <tv-ip> > cytv-diagnose.txt

diagnose.sh logs in as root over SSH (key authentication, as set up by the Homebrew Channel) and only reads: the Share log report, the foreground and running apps, the media pipelines, the processes, the Input key mode, the configuration with secrets hidden, the themes on the TV, the service's last operations and the Live TV status. It changes nothing. Open the file and remove anything private. 2. Give the assistant the context. Start the conversation with AGENTS.md (what the project is, where the TV keeps things, what has gone wrong before, the rules) and the report. Tools that read the repository (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar) pick AGENTS.md up by themselves when you open the folder you cloned. 3. Ask for a diagnosis, not a fix. See the prompts below. Ask it to name the evidence in the report for each conclusion. 4. Try what it suggests, one step at a time, and tell it what happened. If it is a real bug, open an issue with the report and the assistant's findings, or go on with Part 2.

items.title: Prompts
items.text:
Diagnose a report

I use CleanYourTV on an LG webOS TV. Read AGENTS.md first. Below is a diagnostic report (tools/diagnose.sh) and this is what is wrong: describe it: what you did, what you expected, what happened, how often. Work out the most likely causes from the report. For each, quote the lines of the report that support it, and say what would show that it is wrong. Propose read-only checks first. Do not suggest a change to the TV without the exact command, what it does and the command that undoes it. Do not ask me for secrets.

Check the TV live (an agent with SSH)

You may run read-only commands on my TV with ssh root@<tv-ip> (cat, ls, ps, curl to 127.0.0.1:8765, luna-send queries with </dev/null). Do not change, restart, install, delete or reboot anything without asking me first, and name the undo command. Start from AGENTS.md and tools/diagnose.sh. The problem: describe it. Tell me what you found and what you would try next.

Understand the code behind a symptom

Using AGENTS.md ("Where things are") find the code responsible for symptom in this repository. Explain how it works on webOS ⅚ (Node 8.12) and on webOS 25, and list what could make it fail on a TV that is not the maintainer's.

items.title: Part 2: fix the bug and send the fix
items.text:
You need a copy of the repository on your computer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an assistant that can edit files and run commands (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot agent mode and similar). The project's rules are in AGENTS.md; the assistant reads them.

  1. Fork and clone, and make a branch: git checkout -b fix-short-description.
  2. Reproduce the bug. From the report, then from the code. Many bugs can be reproduced without a TV: the service runs under sh tools/check.sh (the tests under Node 8.12.0, as on webOS 5 and 6, and the current Node), and the launcher page runs in Chrome against a stand-in service (see tools/theme-preview.mjs for the idea).
  3. Write a test that fails, then fix the code until it passes. A test in tools/test/ is expected whenever the bug can be tested without a TV. Keep to the compatibility rules (Node 8.12 for the service, ES5 style for the pages).
  4. Run everything: sh tools/check.sh, and python3 ipk/build.py to check that the package builds.
  5. Try it on a TV if you can: once your change is merged into dev it is in the dev build (the pre-release dev); in the manager app Update channel > Dev builds installs it, and Update channel > Stable releases goes back. A branch of your own can be installed by hand: build it with python3 ipk/build.py, copy the .ipk to the TV and run install.sh with CYTV_IPK=/path/to/package.ipk. Say in the pull request what you checked on a TV and what you did not.
  6. Open a pull request with the template. Describe the cause, not only the change, and say that AI tools were used.

What a pull request needs: the tests pass under Node 8.12, a new test for the bug where possible, the documentation page changed when the behaviour changed, no private data (addresses, tokens, playlist URLs, names), an honest note on what was verified on a real TV, and a line saying which AI tools helped. It is reviewed like any other pull request.

items.title: Prompts
items.text:
Fix a bug

Read AGENTS.md. Issue: paste the issue text and the masked report. Reproduce the problem (a failing test in tools/test/ if it can be tested without a TV), find the cause, and make the smallest fix that follows the rules in AGENTS.md (Node 8.12 for the service, ES5 style for the pages, no private data). Run sh tools/check.sh and python3 ipk/build.py. Update the documentation if behaviour changes. Do not commit to main, do not release. Tell me what is verified and what only a real TV can verify.

Review a change

Review my change against AGENTS.md: Node 8.12 compatibility, ES5 style in the pages, private data, missing tests, documentation that no longer matches, and anything that could leave a TV in a state it cannot recover from (boot scripts, mounts, the update path).

Write the pull request text

From the diff, write a pull request description: the symptom, the cause, what changed, how it was tested (name the commands), what was checked on a real TV and what was not, and a line that AI tools were used.

items.title: What the assistant should not do
items.text:
• Run commands on your TV that change it, without asking you first.
  • Paste your tokens, playlist address, IP addresses or names into an issue or a pull request.
  • Release, tag or force-push. The maintainer releases.
  • Copy code from GPL projects into this MIT project.

items.title: Notes for maintainers
items.text: AGENTS.md (and CLAUDE.md, which points to it) is the briefing; keep it short and correct when the layout, the TV facts or the rules change. The issue form asks for the Share log and, if used, the assistant's findings; the pull request template asks for the checks above.

items.title: Service API
items.text:
The service runs as root on 127.0.0.1:8765 and answers JSON. It is what the launcher, the manager and the other apps use, and you can call it from a shell on the TV (for example over SSH).

Who may call it

Requests from web pages with an http(s) origin are refused, so a page opened in the TV's browser cannot drive the service. Local apps and scripts (no Origin header) are accepted.

Endpoint Purpose GET /api/apps Installed apps, config, usage, version POST /api/launch {id, params} Launch an app GET /api/inputs HDMI inputs and their state GET /api/running, POST /api/running/close {id} or {all: true} The running apps the launcher can close, and closing them (only listed apps; never Home or CleanYourTV's own apps) POST /api/notify Picture notification (on the network: POST :8767/notify with the token) GET /api/voice/status, POST /api/voice/install, /uninstall, /set, /listen, /ask, /forget, /ha-test, /ha-agents Optional voice function and AI chat GET /api/theme/list, POST /api/theme/set, /revert Themes for the home screen; see Themes GET /api/wallpapers/status, /list, /photo/<u\|i>/<id>; POST /api/wallpapers/set {size}, /pair, /sync, /remove-uploads, /disconnect Wallpapers: the photo library, the phone page and the Immich sync; see Wallpapers GET /api/live/status, /api/live/channels, /api/live/epg Live TV data POST /api/live/settings, /api/live/refresh, /api/live/reset Live TV setup GET /api/manager/status Versions, updates, options, hook state GET /api/version The service's version GET /api/tv What the service found out about this TV and the decisions that follow from it (Input key mode, notification window, tested firmware) GET /api/service The service's version, its Node.js version and which parts are running (a part that failed to load is listed with the reason)

items.title: Examples
items.text:
# launch an app
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/launch -d '{"id":"com.palm.app.settings"}'

# show a picture notification without a token (from the TV itself)
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/notify -d '{"title":"Hello","text":"From a shell","seconds":8}'

# the service version and updates
curl -s localhost:8765/api/manager/status

See the pages for Live TV, Picture notifications and Voice for their bodies.

items.title: Design
items.text:
The home-screen design follows the Android TV project CleanYourTV (MIT). No code from it is used.

The Glass theme and the theme settings it uses (a glass focus plate that glides between tiles, the name of the focused app under its tile, a name that slides when the focus moves, a light clock with a divider, a soft glow around the dock, the header stepping aside for the grid) take their ideas from the launcher of Clean Your TV for LG webOS by Razdva122 (MIT). They are written anew for this launcher; no code, image or other file from that project is used.

items.title: This documentation
items.text: Built with Zensical.

items.title: Debloat
items.text: An optional clean-up of LG's ads and telemetry. It is on by default in the setup; the manager app has a Debloat screen with its four groups.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
About a minute after every boot, the debloat:

Group What it does Ads Prevents admanager and adoverlay-service from starting, and adds eic.ads.lgtvcommon.com, nl.ad.lgsmartad.com and nl.info.lgsmartad.com to /etc/hosts, pointing at 127.0.0.1 and ::1 and marked # cleanyourtv-debloat (other entries are untouched). Viewing tracking (LivePlus) Prevents acr2 from starting: it recognises what is on screen and reports it. Telemetry logs Stops the systemd services remotelogger and service-logger. Suggestions and nudges Stops contentminer and nudge, and prevents sportsalarm from starting.

A program is prevented from starting by mounting a do-nothing stub over it (in RAM; the real files are not changed). Where /etc/hosts is on the read-only system partition, a copy with the ad lines is kept in RAM (/tmp/cleanyourtv-hosts) and mounted over it until the next restart. Each group can be switched on or off on its own; the ones that are off are listed in options.debloatOff in config.json.

Nothing is uninstalled. It applies only while the launcher is Home, because LG's own Home needs some of those services to start; switching back to LG's Home lifts the debloat first.

items.title: Turning it off
items.text: Switch a group off in the manager app (Debloat), or Switch all off. It starts that group's services again, unmounts its stubs and, for Ads, removes the marked hosts lines. Switching the last group off switches the debloat off. To pause it without the manager, create /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE-DEBLOAT.

items.title: What it does not do
items.text: It does not block updates: firmware update blocking (for example with the Homebrew Channel's tools) is separate and is not touched. It does not claim to remove all tracking. It stops the services listed above and nothing else.

items.title: About this fork
items.text:
This is LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS, a fork of lasharor/cleanyourtv-WebOS. CleanYourTV for LG webOS (the launcher, the root service, Live TV, the Input key, notifications, voice, themes, wallpapers, the debloat and the manager app) is the work of lasharor and its contributors; all credit for it goes to them. The home-screen design follows the Android TV project CleanYourTV. Both are MIT licensed, and so is this fork.

The fork stays close to upstream and adds a few things on top.

items.title: What the fork adds
items.text: Area What Read more Screensaver Your photos full screen with the time and the date when Home is left alone, instead of LG's clock screensaver. Left and Right step through them. Screensaver Photo feed A small, documented, read-only feed any server can offer: the TV fetches one photo at a time and keeps at most 30, never the whole library. family-calendar offers one with its Frameo photos. The photo feed contract Glass theme and UI A Glass theme, a focus that glides between tiles, the app name under the focused grid tile and a name that slides, clock and greeting typography, and Up/Down that land on the tile above or below and go straight back. Ideas from Razdva122/clean-your-tv-lg-webos (MIT); no code was copied. Themes, The launcher Security From an audit of the whole repository: our apps send a per-install API token a web page cannot read, the service answers only requests addressed to 127.0.0.1/localhost, picture downloads cannot reach the TV through a name, and every GitHub Action is pinned to a commit. Security Updates A TV set up from this fork updates only from this fork (releases, themes and the compatibility list), and releases are made by hand from reviewed code, not every night. Updating

items.title: Installing from this fork
items.text:
The same as upstream, with this repository's addresses: in the Homebrew Channel add https://github.com/LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS/releases/latest/download/apps.json, or over SSH:

ssh root@<tv-ip> 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS/main/install.sh | CYTV_REPO=LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS sh'

A TV that already runs upstream's CleanYourTV is moved to the fork by the SSH line above (it also keeps the TV on the fork).

items.title: Upstream
items.text: Changes from upstream are brought in by a reviewed merge, never by the TV itself. Problems with this fork, and with what it adds, go in this fork's issues; security problems privately through a security advisory. Questions about CleanYourTV in general, and the community, are best at upstream and its Discord; the issues and pull requests the documentation links to by number are upstream's.

items.title: The Input key
items.text:
The remote's Input button opens an Inputs picker over the running app.

The picker shows the dock apps in a row, with a green dot on the ones that are open when that is switched on in the launcher's Customise, the inputs below (each with its port and what is connected, and a green dot on the active one) and, when Live TV is on, Live TV. A device's name wraps onto a second line, with an ellipsis at the end of that line when it is longer still, so a long name (HDMI-CEC ones can be) never runs over the cards beside it.

Key Action Left / Right Move Up / Down Switch rows OK Open Hold OK on an HDMI input Put it on Home as a tile, or take it off again (An input on Home) Back or Input Close

The pointer works too.

items.title: What the key shows
items.text:
The Input button can show the Inputs list in three ways. Input key > Input key shows in the manager app chooses; each press of that row goes to the next one.

Choice What happens Default Over the running app, ready in the background A small app, com.cleanyourtv.picker, is started hidden after boot and the key only wakes it: instant. webOS 25 (SDK 10) Over the running app, started when pressed The same app is started by the key and closes itself after use (Back, a choice, or ten idle seconds). Nothing runs hidden, so it cannot keep the remote. The first moment takes longer. every other webOS version (5, 6, and 26 until the background app has been tried there) The launcher's Inputs list The TV goes to Home with the Inputs list open. Needs CleanYourTV as Home; when LG's Home is selected the key stays with LG. none

On webOS 6.5 (reports) the hidden background app kept the remote and showed a loading circle, which is why older webOS starts it on demand. The background app is only kept while the hook attached: without the hook the key cannot open it. If the TV closes the background app three times in ten minutes, the service switches to started when pressed by itself (picker.mode: ondemand in config.json). Other overlay projects for rooted TVs also start their overlay on demand and close it after use.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
It uses the bundled inputhook library, which injects a small hook into LG's input process so that a remote button can run a command. The Input button's code is 241 by default. The command opens the picker app (com.cleanyourtv.picker) over whatever is on screen.

The hook goes into lginput2, LG's input service, where the remote's keys arrive on webOS 5 and newer. Other processes (micomservice and a few more) are only used on firmware without lginput2: hooked into micomservice, the hook replaced a function that process also uses to pass the remote's keys on to HDMI-CEC devices and the soundbar, and after a boot the remote no longer controlled a set-top box and eARC stopped working (issue 23).

items.title: Learning your remote's code
items.text:
Remotes differ. In the manager app, Input key > Learn the Input key reads the code of the button you press and tests that the picker opens. Clear restores the default.

The switch in the same menu removes the bind and gives the button back to LG's own picker. The optional Learn the Home key is under CleanYourTV as Home.

The Guide button can be bound the same way; that is part of Live TV (manager app > Live TV > Learn the Guide key).

When the hook is not attached

On some firmware the hook cannot attach. The manager then shows the Input key as not available and LG's picker is used.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
1. Root the TV and install the Homebrew Channel (rootmy.tv).
  2. Install the CleanYourTV manager app: from the Homebrew Channel, or from your computer with the install command and the TV's IP address (below).
  3. On the TV, open CleanYourTV and choose Set up now. It takes about a minute and the screen blinks once.

That is all. The launcher is LG's Home from then on.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• An LG webOS TV rooted with the Homebrew Channel.
  • SSH access to the TV as root, which the Homebrew Channel can enable (Settings > SSH Server).
  • Internet access on the TV (the install command downloads the package from GitHub).
  • webOS 5 or newer (2020 models and later). webOS 4 and older are not supported: they have no systemd and an old Node.js, and the setup stops before it changes anything.
  • Firmware from the tested TVs, or one where LG's Home app is of the flutter or web kind; see What happens on unlisted firmware.

Give the TV a fixed address

Reserve a fixed IP address for the TV in your router so the install command and the network notification address never change.

items.title: From the Homebrew Channel
items.text:
Add CleanYourTV's repository to the Homebrew Channel once: open the Homebrew Channel, the gear at the top, Add repository, and enter

https://github.com/LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS/releases/latest/download/apps.json

CleanYourTV then shows in the channel's list: open it and choose Install. A new release shows there as an update. The package is the same file as in Releases, checked against its SHA-256.

items.title: From your computer
items.text:
With your TV's IP address:

ssh root@192.168.1.50 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS/main/install.sh | sh'

The script downloads the latest release package, checks its SHA-256 and installs it. Nothing else on the TV changes in this step. The package can also be downloaded from Releases and installed with the Homebrew Channel or ares-install.

items.title: 2. Set up, on the TV
items.text:
Open CleanYourTV from the app list, choose the options and Set up now.

Option Default Debloat LG's ads and telemetry on Take over the Input key on

The setup:

  1. saves the original state in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/backup;
  2. installs the launcher and the service;
  3. adds boot scripts to /var/lib/webosbrew/init.d/;
  4. replaces LG's Home at boot (in RAM) and starts the service;
  5. checks that the new Home came up. If it did not, it removes the boot scripts and restarts the TV with LG's Home.

Its log is /media/developer/cytv-setup.log, kept across the restart, with the service log next to it in cytv-setup.log.service.

The same setup over SSH 

sh /media/developer/apps/usr/palm/services/com.cleanyourtv.manager.service/bootstrap.sh install
Options: --no-debloat, --no-input-key, --no-start, --no-verify, --force.

items.title: Unlisted firmware
items.text: The setup matches the TV's firmware against compat.json (it fetches the newest copy from the repository and falls back to the one in the package). A listed firmware is set up directly. For an unlisted firmware the setup continues when LG's Home app is the flutter or web kind, and otherwise stops and offers Set up anyway. On a TV whose Home is LG's native program (webOS 5 to 23) the launcher becomes Home through a stand-in, see what differs between webOS versions. To add a firmware to the list, open an issue with the output of Share log (Troubleshooting).

items.title: Installing a dev build
items.text: To try a change that is not released yet, install the dev build: see Updating and uninstalling.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• The Home button opens LG's full-screen Home, not CleanYourTV. Some TVs have a Home Style setting. Set TV Settings > General > Home Settings > Home Style to Basic.
  • FAILED_IPKG_INSTALL. Remove the com.cleanyourtv.manager entry marked half-installed from /media/developer/apps/var/lib/opkg/status and install again.
  • Black screen after switching or rebooting. Wait a minute; if it stays black, restart the TV.

More in Troubleshooting.

items.title: Languages
items.text: CleanYourTV's screens are in English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish, Russian, Turkish and Arabic: the launcher, its menus and Live TV, the manager app, the Inputs list, and the pages a phone opens from a QR code (Wallpapers, Live TV setup, voice setup, Share log).

items.title: Choosing the language
items.text: Where Language The TV's screens The TV's menu language. In the manager app, More > Language can choose another one: Automatic follows the TV again. The list shows how much of each language is translated; what is missing stays English. Dates and the clock follow the same choice. A phone page The phone's own language, then the one chosen in the manager, then English. The Share log report Always English, because it is read by the people who look into a bug report.

items.title: Adding or improving a language
items.text:
The Russian, Turkish and Arabic translations were machine-made and have not been reviewed by a native speaker yet; corrections are very welcome.

Translations are plain text files in the repository, one per language, so no programming is needed. Anyone can add a language or fix a translation with a pull request; the next release then brings it to every TV.

  1. Open i18n/en.json. It lists every English text the screens use, as "English text": "English text".
  2. Copy it to i18n/<code>.json, where <code> is the two-letter code of the language (it for Italian, pl for Polish). Set _name to the language's name in that language ("Italiano") and _dir to ltr, or rtl for a right-to-left language.
  3. Replace each value with the translation. Leave out a line you are not sure about: that text stays English. Translating the texts of the launcher and the menus first gives the most visible result.
  4. Keep the placeholders: %s is filled in with a text (a name, a version) and %d with a number, in the same order as in English.
  5. A text with a number can have plural forms, as "%d photos": {"one": "%d foto", "other": "%d foto’s"}. The forms are the Unicode CLDR plural categories (zero, one, two, few, many, other); other is required, and the form follows the first number in the text.
  6. Keep translations short where you can: the TV is read from a few metres away, and a text too long for its row or button ends in "...".
  7. Open a pull request against the dev branch. If you cannot use git, open a New language issue and attach the file.

The checks of the pull request run node tools/i18n.js: it shows how complete each language is, and it fails only when a file is not valid JSON or a placeholder does not match the English text. To try a language on a TV before it is released, install the dev build once the pull request is merged.

items.title: Right-to-left languages
items.text: With "_dir": "rtl" (Arabic, Hebrew) the home screen, its menus, the Inputs list and the manager app are mirrored, and Left and Right on the remote follow the mirrored layout. Live TV keeps its left-to-right layout for now. Arabic is the first right-to-left language.

items.title: For developers
items.text: New texts are written in English and passed through t('...') in the launcher and the picker, tr() in the manager, and i18n.tr() in the service's phone pages. node tools/i18n.js --sync adds texts from t('...') calls to en.json, and node tools/build-pages.js puts each page's translations into it. i18n/README.md has the details.

items.title: The launcher
items.text: The launcher replaces LG's Home. It is a web page of the project that the TV's browser runs, so it starts fast and works the same on every supported webOS version.

items.title: The screen
items.text:
• Dock. Up to four apps, large, on the first row.
  • Top shelf. The name of the focused app and an ambient glow taken from its icon.
  • Grid. All other apps, sorted by how often you use each one (or A to Z).
  • Top buttons. Inputs, Live TV, Settings and Customise, and a clock. The buttons you see are yours to change.
  • Open apps. Optionally a green dot on the tile of every app that is open, as on the active input in the Inputs list: off by default, Customise > Mark running apps switches it on, in the launcher and in the Inputs picker. Back on the home screen lists the open apps to close them (see Running apps).

items.title: Keys
items.text:
Action How Open an app OK Move between the rows Up and Down go to the app or button above or below; the opposite key right after goes straight back to where the focus was App options (dock, hide) Hold OK on an app Move or remove a top button Hold OK on it Customise The Customise button Live TV The Live TV button or tile Switch input The Inputs button Put an input on Home Hold OK on it in the Inputs list Close running apps Back on the home screen

The Magic Remote pointer works too: pointing and clicking, and holding the button on an app for its options.

items.title: Running apps
items.text:
Back on the home screen lists the apps that are open, as LG's Home does with its Recents on a second Back. OK closes an app, Close all closes every app in the list, and Back leaves it. Closing an app also removes it from LG's recent apps.

It lists the apps the launcher knows, including the ones you hid from the grid; Home itself, CleanYourTV's own apps and the TV's system apps are never in it. The list is read when it opens and closes when you leave Home. Suggested and first built by Steefzar.

items.title: Customise
items.text:
Customise holds how Home looks:

  • the dock: each app in it can be replaced (an app already in the dock swaps places), moved or removed, and Add an app... fills a free place. Holding OK on an app gives Add to dock, Move left, Move right, Remove from dock and Hide app;
  • the top buttons: move one left or right, remove it, or add Inputs, Settings, Live TV or any app;
  • hidden apps (show them again);
  • the app order (most used first, or A to Z);
  • mark running apps (a green dot on their tiles, or none);
  • the clock format (automatic, 12 or 24 hour);
  • the theme (see Themes) and the accent colour; the theme list shows each theme's screenshot;
  • Wallpapers: your own photos behind Home, and how often they change (see Wallpapers);
  • More settings..., which opens the manager app for everything the TV and the service do.

Putting the dock, buttons, hidden apps, order and clock back to the defaults is in the manager app: Reset Home customisation.

items.title: Inputs
items.text: The Inputs button lists HDMI inputs by the names LG shows, with what is connected and a marker on the active one. OK switches to the input.

items.title: An input on Home
items.text:
Hold OK on an input in the Inputs list and choose Add to Home. The input then shows as a tile, with the HDMI symbol, the name the TV gives it (for example the name of the connected console) and its port. It is a tile like an app: OK switches to the input, and holding OK on it offers Add to dock, Move left, Move right and Remove from dock. Remove from Home takes it off again; that is also in the Inputs list. A tile of an input with nothing connected is dimmed and still switches to it.

In the Inputs picker of the Input key, holding OK on an HDMI input does the same: it is added to Home, or taken off when it already is. An input in the dock also shows in the picker's row of dock apps.

Suggested and first built by ibexes.

items.title: Icons
items.text:
Each tile uses the app's own icon. The tile colour is taken from the icon's edge colour, so an icon that reaches its edges blends into the tile, and the ambient glow comes from the icon's most vivid colour. Colours are worked out once per app and remembered.

An icon that is an opaque square with a transparent margin around it (many LG icons) is enlarged so it fills its tile, and a gradient icon in the dock gets a tile with the same gradient (#3).

items.title: Language
items.text: Menus follow the TV's language, or the one chosen in the manager app: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish, Russian, Turkish and Arabic. See Languages, also for adding one.

items.title: Themes
items.text: The look of the home screen (colours, tile and text size, columns, clock, glow, animation speed, wallpaper) is a theme, chosen in the manager app.

items.title: Settings file
items.text:
Settings are stored on the TV in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/config.json:

Key Meaning dock App ids in the dock (up to four). topbar The buttons at the top. hidden App ids you hid. pinnedInputs The inputs on Home: {id, label, port}, id being the input's app (for example com.webos.app.hdmi2). sort usage or alpha. clock auto, 12 or 24. runDots true shows a green dot on open apps (off by default).

See config.example.json. Change settings in the launcher; the file is read and written by the service.

items.title: Live TV
items.text: Plays an IPTV playlist (M3U) from your own provider or server. It does not use LG's tuner, and the project provides no channels and no playlist.

items.title: Setting it up
items.text:
On first use the screen shows an address and a 6-digit code.

  1. Open the address on a phone or computer on the same network as the TV.
  2. Enter the code.
  3. Paste your M3U playlist address (and the XMLTV guide address if the playlist does not carry one).

The page closes by itself. It is open for ten minutes at most and only with the code.

From a shell on the TV instead:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/live/settings -d '{"playlistUrl":"http://...","epgUrl":"http://..."}'

items.title: Turning it off
items.text: Live TV is optional. In the manager app, Live TV > Show Live TV switches it on and off. Off hides it everywhere: the Live TV button and tile in the launcher, Live TV in the Inputs list, and the Guide key takeover (below). LG's own player and guide are used as before. The playlist and your favourites are kept, so switching it on again brings them back.

items.title: Keys
items.text:
Key Watching In the guide (OK) Up / Down, CH+ / CH- Next / previous channel Move; CH+ / CH- page Left / Right Channel banner (now and next) Previous / next tab Digits Jump to a channel number (playlist order) Same OK Open the guide Play the channel Guide Open the guide Close the guide Green Add / remove favourite Add / remove favourite Yellow Player menu (favourite, stream, statistics) Filters Blue Statistics Red Search (the TV's keyboard) Back Return to the launcher Clear filters and search, then close the guide

The tabs are All channels, Favourites, Recent and one per category of your playlist. Channels show badges for country, language and quality when the playlist names them (for example NL, EN, HD). Filters narrow the list by country, language and quality; search matches names across all channels.

items.title: The Guide button
items.text: By default the remote's Guide button belongs to LG. In the manager app, Live TV > Learn the Guide key records the button's code; afterwards it opens the Live TV channel guide over whatever is running, and closes it again when Live TV is open. Clear gives LG's guide back. The button is only taken over while Live TV is on and a code is learned. It uses the same hook as the Input key.

items.title: How it plays
items.text:
• The TV's own player plays HLS (.m3u8).
  • Stepping through channels with Up/Down starts the new channel only when the keys have paused for 180 ms. Channels you skip are never requested from your provider, which matters for accounts that allow one connection.
  • The player uses one video element for the whole session instead of creating one per channel.
  • The guide (XMLTV) is refreshed twice a day and keeps 36 hours.
  • The guide address can be an .xml or .xml.gz file. When the field is empty, the address in the playlist (url-tvg or x-tvg-url) is used; for an Xtream playlist (…/get.php?username=…&password=…) it is the provider's xmltv.php on the same server.
  • A playlist channel gets its programmes from the guide channel with the same tvg-id. When there is none, the channel's name is compared with the guide channel's names, ignoring case, accents, a leading country code (PL:, NL|), quality words (HD, FHD, 4K) and punctuation, so PL: TVP 1 HD matches TVP 1.
  • An Xtream link ending in .ts (…/live/<user>/<password>/<id>.ts) is played as it is first. The provider's HLS (.m3u8) and a .ts marked as HLS are tried after it, because on webOS 5 and 6 they can stall for 15 seconds before the next try starts.
  • When a playlist lists the same channel in several qualities (for example HD and SD), they are merged into one channel with several streams. If one does not start, the next is tried; a stream that stalls is reloaded once.
  • When a channel does not play, the screen says why: the server refused it, the stream is gone, it needs DRM, it is not video, or it is too slow.
  • Statistics (Blue) show the resolution, buffer, dropped frames and which stream is playing.

There is no recording and no pause.

items.title: Where it is stored
items.text:
The playlist address, which usually contains an access key, is stored only on the TV, in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/live/, readable by root only. To clear it:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/live/reset

Favourites, recent channels and the failed-channel list are stored in state.json in the same folder.

items.title: The manager app
items.text:
CleanYourTV in LG's app list sets up, updates and removes everything. The left side of the screen explains the focused row.

Row Function Launcher, Service Installed version; offers an update when the latest release is newer. Check for updates Asks GitHub for the latest release. Update channel Follow the stable releases or the dev builds. Go back to launcher Appears after a launcher update. CleanYourTV as Home Use CleanYourTV as Home (LG's Home or ours; the TV restarts) and the optional Learn the Home key. Wallpapers Your own photos behind Home: the phone page (uploads and Immich), counts, Sync now, Picture size, Remove all uploads and Disconnect Immich. See Wallpapers. Live TV Show Live TV (off hides it in the launcher and Inputs list and leaves the Guide button to LG), the Playlist (set up from your phone with a QR code and a 6-digit code), Refresh playlist and guide, Learn the Guide key, Clear recent channels and Remove the playlist. See Live TV. Input key The takeover switch, Learn the Input key, Input key shows (the Inputs list over the running app, ready in the background or started when pressed, or the launcher's own list). See The Input key. Debloat The four groups of the debloat, each on or off, and Switch all on / Switch all off. More Language: the language of every screen, Automatic (the TV's) or one of the translations with how complete it is; see Translations. Voice: optional; installs the speech recogniser (about 80 MB), learns the voice button, tries it, sets where the text goes (see Voice). Network notifications: switch, address, token (also as a QR code for a phone) and an example for sending picture notifications from other devices. Share log A QR code that opens a masked diagnostic report on a phone, with a Copy button. Reset Home customisation Puts the launcher's dock, top buttons, hidden apps, app order and clock back to the defaults, after a confirmation. The theme stays. Uninstall Removes everything and restarts the TV.

items.title: When the service is not running
items.text: The manager works without the service for two things: checking for a newer package and installing it, so a broken service can be repaired from the TV. It follows the same Update channel as the service: on the dev channel it offers the dev build's package. Set up now starts from the options that are already saved (Input key, Debloat), so setting up again does not switch them back on.

items.title: Share log
items.text:
Share log opens a short-lived page on your local network (port 8768 or higher, a random address, ten minutes). Scan the QR code with a phone on the same network. It works even when the service is not running, so it can also report a failed setup.

The report is masked: addresses, MAC addresses and URL paths are replaced, and the values of token, key, password, pass, secret and apikey are removed. It holds the TV model and firmware, the versions, LG's stock Home app, the mounts and boot scripts, whether our apps are registered, your options, the remote key codes seen by the input hook, the service status, the setup log, the last lines of the service log and the input hook log. Attach it to bug reports.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
Open CleanYourTV. The launcher (the home screen) and the service (the background part) update separately from the latest GitHub release, each checked against its SHA-256 file.

  • A launcher that does not start is replaced by the previous one, and a service that does not start by the previous files.
  • Go back to launcher returns to the previous launcher version after an update.
  • Before the setup, the app offers a newer package by itself.
  • Running the install command again also updates.
  • An update from the Homebrew Channel (or ares-install) installs the package only; the service notices the new package within about four minutes and takes it into use, as an update from the app does. A version whose start failed once is not tried again.

items.title: Update channel
items.text:
Update channel in the manager app chooses where updates come from.

Channel What it follows Stable releases The latest published release, made by hand from reviewed changes on dev. This is the default. Dev builds Every change, as soon as it is on the dev branch: for people who want fixes early or are asked to try one.

items.title: Dev builds
items.text:
All work lands on the dev branch. Every push to it builds the package (.github/workflows/dev-build.yml) and publishes it as the pre-release named dev, replacing the one before. When a release is made, the release workflow turns what is on dev into the next stable release. The stable updater never sees pre-releases.

Follow the dev builds Update channel > Dev builds (it shows the commit and date), then install with the Launcher and Service rows. Expect updates several times a day. Back to the stable releases Update channel > Stable releases. The stable release is offered again, also when it is older than the dev build. Install from scratch ssh root@<tv-ip> 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LanceSandino/cleanyourtv-WebOS/main/install.sh \| CYTV_CHANNEL=dev sh'. The manager then follows the dev builds. Same version number A dev build records its commit in a BUILD file, so a newer push of the same version is still offered. Old test builds Before service 1.6.9 every branch had its own test build (test-<branch>). A TV that followed one follows the dev builds now.

A dev build can be less finished than a release

It is checked against its SHA-256 file like any release, but nobody has signed it. See Security.

items.title: Switching between LG's Home and the launcher
items.text:
Switching restarts the TV (about a minute).

Action How Use LG's Home CleanYourTV as Home off in the manager app. Use the launcher again CleanYourTV as Home on, from LG's app list. Over SSH touch /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE; reboot for LG's Home, rm /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE; reboot for ours. Failed boot The Homebrew Channel's failsafe mode skips all boot scripts; reboot again.

While LG's Home is selected the service still runs, so the manager app and the Input key keep working.

items.title: Uninstalling
items.text:
Uninstall in the manager app, or over SSH:

sh /media/developer/cleanyourtv/uninstall.sh

--keep-config keeps your settings and usage history, and --no-reboot restores LG's Home right away instead of restarting the TV. Uninstalling removes the apps, boot scripts and Input-key bind and restarts the TV, which then starts with LG's Home. See What it changes on the TV for what is removed.

items.title: Picture notifications
items.text:
The com.cleanyourtv.notify app shows a card (picture, title, text) over whatever is on screen without taking the remote. Other devices send it with a POST request, for example Home Assistant showing a camera snapshot when the doorbell rings.

The pictures on this page are rendered with made-up data (a made-up camera picture and a made-up token), not taken from a real TV or home.

items.title: Enable it
items.text:
In the manager app: Network notifications > Accept notifications from the network. It is off by default.

Row What it does How to send Shows the address, the token and an example request as text on the TV. Show as QR code Shows a QR code for your phone (below). New token Replaces the token; devices that use the old one stop working.

The token is a secret

Anyone who has it and can reach the TV can show cards on its screen. New token replaces it.

items.title: Get the address and the token on your phone
items.text:
The token is 48 characters long. Instead of typing it, scan a QR code:

  1. In the manager app choose Network notifications > Show as QR code.
  2. Scan the code with the camera of a phone that is on the same Wi-Fi as the TV, and open the link.

  1. The page shows the address, the token and the header to send, each with a Copy button. Paste them where you need them (for Home Assistant, see below).

The page is served by the TV itself at a random address (/t/ and 24 random characters) on the notification port. It works for ten minutes after the code was shown, then the address answers like any wrong request. It follows the same allow list as the notification address (see below). It is plain HTTP like the notifications, so the token crosses your Wi-Fi unencrypted: use a network you trust and close the screen on the TV when you are done.

items.title: Sending one
items.text:
curl -X POST http://192.168.1.50:8767/notify \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Front door","text":"Someone is at the door","image":"http://192.168.1.20/snapshot.jpg","seconds":15,"position":"top-right"}'
Field Meaning title, text Up to 120 and 400 characters; either may be empty. image http(s) address of a picture, up to 6 MB. The TV downloads it, so the address must be reachable from the TV. If it cannot be fetched the card still appears and says why. seconds Display time, 2 to 120 (default 8). position top, middle or bottom plus left, center or right (default top-right).

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text:
Add a rest_command (in configuration.yaml; keep the token in secrets.yaml, for example cleanyourtv_bearer: "Bearer <token>"):

rest_command:
  cleanyourtv_notify:
    url: "http://192.168.1.50:8767/notify"
    method: POST
    headers:
      Authorization: !secret cleanyourtv_bearer
      Content-Type: "application/json"
    payload: >-
      {{ {"title": title | default(""), "text": text | default(""), "image": image | default(""),
          "seconds": seconds | default(10), "position": position | default("top-right")} | tojson }}
    timeout: 10

Then call it from an automation. This shows a camera picture when a sensor fires:

actions:
  - action: rest_command.cleanyourtv_notify
    data:
      title: Front door
      text: Someone is at the door
      image: "http://homeassistant.local:8123{{ state_attr('camera.front_door', 'entity_picture') }}"
      seconds: 20

The camera's entity_picture carries a short-lived access token, which is valid right when the card is sent. The TV downloads the picture, so use an address of Home Assistant that the TV can reach. Test with Developer tools > Actions in Home Assistant: a 401 means the token is wrong, a 403 means the allow list blocks Home Assistant's address.

items.title: Limits and safety
items.text:
• The port (default 8767) and an allow list of addresses are in config.json under notifyApi: {"enabled":true,"port":8767,"allow":["192.168.1.0/24"]} (prefixes /8, /16 and /24 are supported).
  • Requests use plain HTTP, so the token is visible to anyone who can watch your network traffic. Keep the TV on a network you trust.
  • Ten wrong tokens lock an address out for ten minutes, and at most 20 notifications a minute are accepted.
  • From a shell on the TV, POST localhost:8765/api/notify accepts the same body without a token.

See Security.

items.title: Screensaver
items.text:
When Home is left alone, CleanYourTV can show your photos full screen with the time and the date, instead of LG's screensaver. It is off until you switch it on in Customise > Screensaver.

Setting What it does Use the screensaver On or off. The line under it says where the photos come from. Starts after 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes without a key or a pointer move on Home. New photo Every 10, 15, 30 or 60 seconds, cross-faded. Time and date Shown at the bottom left, or not. Show it now Starts it at once, to see how it looks.

While it shows, Left and Right step back and forward through the last 50 photos (Right past the last one brings a new photo, and the timer starts again); right-to-left languages mirror them. Any other key or a move of the Magic Remote ends it, and that key does nothing else. Photos are shown whole on black (portrait photos too) and darker from ten at night to seven in the morning. It does not start over Live TV.

LG's screensaver. Before the TV starts its own screensaver it asks the apps that registered for it. While the screensaver is on and there are photos, the launcher answers no and shows the photos instead; otherwise LG's screensaver starts as before. When another app is on the screen (and idle), Home comes forward with the photos, and a key or the pointer goes straight back to that app; the Home key ends them and stays on Home. Whether a TV asks Home at all depends on the firmware: if LG's screensaver still appears, set Starts after shorter than LG's.

items.title: Where the photos come from
items.text:
1. A photo feed, when one is set up (below).
  2. Otherwise the Wallpapers photos (phone uploads and Immich), in a shuffled order.

A photo feed's photos are Wallpapers photos as well: Customise > Wallpapers counts them, shows them behind Home and lets you choose one of them as your wallpaper.

The TV never holds a whole photo library. It reads the feed's list of photo ids every hour and fetches a photo, at 1920 pixels, only when it is about to be shown (and the one after it). Photos are shown from memory (the last 8); only a small offline set goes to the TV's storage: the first 5 at once, then at most one new photo every half hour, at most 20 photos (24 MB), and nothing while the storage has less than 300 MB free. A screensaver that changes photos all evening therefore hardly writes to the TV's flash memory. A photo from the feed chosen as the wallpaper is always kept. Photos come in a shuffled round: every photo once before any comes back, never the same one twice in a row. The round is saved with the list, so after a restart the TV goes on where it was; a photo added on the server joins the current round, and a photo hidden or deleted on the server leaves the TV at the next read of the list. With the server away, the photos already on the TV keep the screensaver going.

items.title: Setting up a photo feed
items.text:
1. On the server that offers the feed, create a token for the TV and copy its setup code (it starts with cyfp1.). The code holds the server's address, a token that can only read the feed, and the server's own root certificate. In family-calendar this is Admin > Photo feeds, on the server itself.
  2. On the TV: Customise > Screensaver > Photo feed... shows a QR code and an address with a 6-digit code. Open it on a phone, or type the address on a computer on the same network (the computer that runs family-calendar works: copy the setup code there and paste it straight in); the page opens on Photo feed. Paste the code and choose Check and save. The code is tried before it is saved. The CleanYourTV app's Wallpapers screen shows the feed (Photo feed: how many photos, when it was read) and can disconnect it.

The token is kept in config.json (readable by root only) and is never shown again or sent to the launcher. The TV talks to the server over HTTPS only, trusts only the certificate in the code, and follows no redirects. To stop, choose Disconnect the photo feed on the phone page (its photos leave the TV), and revoke the token on the server.

Over SSH the same works on the TV itself:

curl -s -X POST 127.0.0.1:8765/api/photofeed/setup -d '{"code":"cyfp1...."}'
curl -s 127.0.0.1:8765/api/photofeed/status

items.title: The photo feed contract
items.text:
Any server can offer a photo feed; the TV needs only these two calls and a setup code. Everything is HTTPS, and every request carries Authorization: Bearer <token> with a token that can do nothing but read the feed.

Call Answer GET /api/feed/photos 200 {"stamp": "...", "photos": [{"id": "...", "createdAt": "..."}]}: the photos to show, newest first, with ETag; 304 for a matching If-None-Match. Ids are 1-64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -. GET /api/feed/photos/<id>?w=1920 200 image/jpeg: the photo upright, fitted inside w x w without enlarging, metadata removed (w is 1280, 1920 or 2560). 404 for a photo that is gone or hidden, 422 for one the server cannot convert: the TV skips both.

A refused token is 401; the TV then keeps showing what it has and says so on the phone page. The setup code is cyfp1. and base64url (no padding) of the JSON {"u": "https://<host>[:port]", "t": "<token>", "ca": "<root certificate, base64 DER>"}; ca may be left out for a server with a publicly trusted certificate. The TV sends the address in u exactly as given, also as the Host.

items.title: family-calendar and Frameo
items.text: The first server with a photo feed is family-calendar, which imports a Frameo frame's photos read-only on the server and offers them, with its other photos, as a feed (Admin > Photo feeds). The TV never talks to Frameo or holds the Frameo identity: hiding a photo in family-calendar hides it on the TV too.

items.title: Service API
items.text: Call What it does GET /api/photofeed/status Set up or not, the server's host, the last 4 characters of the token, how many photos, how many on the TV, the last read GET /api/photofeed/next The id of the next photo, already on the TV ({"id": null} when there is none) GET /api/photofeed/photo/<id> That photo (JPEG) POST /api/photofeed/setup {code}, POST /api/photofeed/refresh, POST /api/photofeed/disconnect Set up, read the list now, remove

items.title: What this changes on a TV
items.text:
CleanYourTV runs a service as root on a rooted TV. It listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 only. A few short-lived pages open on the local network on request, and an optional notification endpoint is off by default.

Port What When it is open 8765 (127.0.0.1 only) The service API Always; see Service API 8766 Live TV pairing page While you set up Live TV: a 6-digit code shown on the TV, ten minutes 8767 Network notifications Only when you switch it on in the manager app; needs a token 8768 and up Share-log page Ten minutes, at a random address, with a masked report 8769 Voice setup page Ten minutes, at a random 128-bit address, closed after saving 8791 Wallpapers page While the QR screen is open in the manager app: a 6-digit code shown on the TV, at most an hour; see Wallpapers

What the setup changes on the TV is listed in What it changes on the TV.

items.title: Network notifications
items.text:
Off until switched on in the manager app. It then listens on port 8767 for POST /notify with Authorization: Bearer <token> (a random 192-bit token kept in config.json, readable by root only). It exposes only the notification call. Wrong tokens lock an address out for ten minutes, requests are limited to 20 a minute and 32 KB, and an optional allow list restricts addresses. It is plain HTTP: the token can be read by anyone who can watch the traffic on your network.

Show as QR code in the manager makes the same port serve one more page, GET /t/<24 random characters>, for ten minutes: it shows the address and the token so a phone can copy them. The address is created when the code is shown (96 bits of randomness), follows the same allow list, and stops working after ten minutes, when notifications are switched off or the service restarts. Anyone who sees the code on the screen, or can read the traffic, can read the token while it is open; New token replaces it.

items.title: Themes
items.text: The manager downloads the theme list, screenshots, theme files and wallpapers from raw.githubusercontent.com (the main branch of this repository) over HTTPS, when you open Theme or choose a theme. They are data only: the service checks every value against its list, limits the sizes (theme 32 KB, wallpaper 1.5 MB, screenshot 600 KB), checks that images are images and refuses anything else. There is no script or CSS in a theme. Anything merged into main becomes available to every TV, which is the same trust you place in the releases of this repository; there is no signature.

items.title: Photo feed (screensaver)
items.text: Optional and off until a setup code from a server that offers a photo feed (for example family-calendar) is pasted on the Wallpapers phone page. The service then reads that server's feed over HTTPS only, trusting only the root certificate in the setup code, with a token that can only read the feed; it follows no redirects. The token is kept in config.json (root only) and is never returned by the service or given to the launcher. At most 30 photos (40 MB) are kept on the TV. See Screensaver.

items.title: Voice
items.text:
Optional and off by default. Installing it downloads files over HTTPS from PyPI, Ubuntu's archive and Moonshine's model server; each file is checked against a SHA-256 value written in the code, and a mismatch stops the install. The recogniser is a 64-bit program started by the root service with its own copy of the C library; it reads audio from a pipe and prints text.

  • Audio from the remote's microphone is held in memory only while recognising.
  • Only the recognised text is sent, and only to the address you set (plain http:// is possible: the token is then visible on your network) and, if you switch on AI chat, to openrouter.ai over HTTPS with your OpenRouter key and the model you chose. OpenRouter and that model's provider see the text.
  • The phone setup page is a short-lived page on the local network (port 8769, a random 128-bit address, ten minutes, closed after saving, plain HTTP: the key is visible on the network while it is typed).
  • With Home Assistant set up, the recognised text goes to the address you set, with your long-lived access token (plain http:// is possible: the token is then visible on your network; a self-signed certificate is accepted only when you switch that on).
  • The keys and the token are kept in config.json (readable by root only) and are never returned by the service.
  • Pausing LG's voice assistant sends it SIGSTOP; nothing of LG's is modified.

items.title: Trust
items.text: Everything it installs comes from this repository's GitHub releases and runs as root. Releases carry a SHA-256 file, which detects corruption but not a compromised repository. Download only from the release page of this repository.

items.title: Dev builds
items.text: The manager's Update channel can follow the dev builds: the pre-release named dev that GitHub Actions publishes for each push to the dev branch. It is opt-in and off by default; the stable updater only reads the latest non-pre-release. A dev build is downloaded over HTTPS from the repository the TV already updates from and checked against the .sha256 file in the same release, so the check protects against a damaged download, not against someone who can publish to the repository (the same is true of stable releases, which are not signed yet). The only pre-release the updater reads is the one tagged dev, and the files must be the package and launcher names the updater already expects.

items.title: Limits to know about
items.text:
• Any app on the TV can already run root commands through the Homebrew Channel; apps are not a security boundary on a rooted TV.
  • /media/developer is world-writable on webOS. The setup removes group and other write access from this project's files and keeps the playlist and settings files owner-only, but the parent folder remains writable.
  • The service API refuses requests from web pages (any http(s) origin) and requests addressed to any name but 127.0.0.1 or localhost (DNS rebinding). A web page can hide its origin (a sandboxed frame sends null, as our own apps do), so our apps also send an API token: a random value the service keeps for root only and writes as cytv-token.js into the launcher, the manager and the picker, where a web page cannot read it. Once every app has it and one has sent it back, a request with origin null and no token is refused; until then (or when an app could not get it) the service accepts it as before, so a TV keeps working. Programs on the TV (scripts, curl) send no origin and need no token.
  • A notification picture is downloaded only from an address that is not the TV itself, checked again after the name is looked up.

Move from telnet to SSH

A rooted TV often has an unauthenticated telnet server open on the local network. Turn telnet off and SSH on in the Homebrew Channel's settings.

items.title: Reporting
items.text: Open a private security advisory on the GitHub repository, or an issue that does not include exploit details.

items.title: webOS version numbers
items.text:
LG names its webOS versions in two ways: a marketing name and the version the TV reports to software. The SDK version (Settings > About, or sdkVersion in the setup log) is the second one and is what the setup reads.

Marketing name First shipped on SDK version reported webOS 5 2020 5.x webOS 6 2021 6.x webOS 22 2022 7.x webOS 23 2023 8.x webOS 24 2024 9.x webOS 25 2025 10.x webOS 26 2026 11.x

LG also updates older TVs to newer versions, so the SDK version, not the model year, is what counts. The service avoids features the older versions lack: webOS 5 and 6 ship Node.js 8 (and Chromium 79 on webOS 6). The details are in Internals.

items.title: What differs between webOS versions
items.text:
All per-TV decisions are made in one place, helper/tvprofile.js, from the SDK version and the kind of LG's Home app as it came with the TV. Share log and GET /api/tv show what was decided.

The Home row follows LG's Home app, not the version number: a TV with a native Home gets the stand-in whatever its version, and a flutter or web Home gets the mount. How both work is in What it changes on the TV.

items.title: Themes
items.text:
A theme changes how the home screen looks: colours, the size of tiles and text, the number of columns, the clock, the ambient glow, the speed of animations and a wallpaper. Themes apply to the launcher's home screen (dock, top shelf, grid, top buttons and menus). Live TV, the Inputs picker and the notification cards keep their own look.

In the launcher, Customise > Theme lists the themes; choosing one applies it at once (a theme that is not on the TV yet is downloaded first). Go back to the previous theme is at the bottom of the list. Customise > Accent colour sets the colour of the focus ring and of the highlighted button or menu row, on top of any theme. The theme list shows the highlighted theme's screenshot and description. The Inputs picker and the Live TV banner and guide follow the theme's colours, accent and typeface too. Your own photos can replace a theme's background: see Wallpapers.

items.title: Where the themes come from
items.text:
Themes are not part of the service. They are read from the themes/ folder of the GitHub repository (the main branch):

  • The service downloads themes/index.json (the list) when you open Theme.
  • Choosing a theme downloads its theme.json and its wallpaper to the TV (/media/developer/cleanyourtv/themes/<id>/) and keeps them, so it keeps working offline. Choosing it again downloads the latest version. If GitHub cannot be reached, the list shows the themes that are already on the TV and says why.
  • Classic is built into the service and always works.
  • A theme is data only (values, an image): the service checks every value, limits the file sizes (theme 32 KB, wallpaper 1.5 MB, screenshot 600 KB) and checks that the images are images. There is no script or CSS in a theme.

items.title: The themes
items.text:
Theme What it is Classic The original look: near-black, white focus, ten columns. The default. Midnight Deep blue with a wallpaper and a blue focus. OLED black Pure black and no ambient glow, so unlit pixels stay off. Warm Brown and amber, with the glow in the accent colour and a wallpaper. Compact Twelve columns of smaller tiles: more apps on screen. Large print Eight columns of big tiles and larger text. Still No animation and a quiet glow. Bloom A flower wallpaper with the dock in a glass panel at the bottom. Down moves the dock up and the apps appear below it, centred. Horizon A row of seven square apps along the bottom of a dusk landscape, the clock on the left and the buttons on the right at the top. Down moves the row up and shows all apps below it. Pixel Pixel art: a blocky typeface, square tiles and buttons, a yellow focus box and a sunset over a lake drawn in big pixels. Moves without animation, like an old console. Lock Screen A phone-style lock screen: a greeting and a big clock top left, and a small, translucent dock low in the corner over a calm blue landscape, so the picture fills the screen. Down moves the dock up and shows all apps below it. Turn Wallpapers on for your own photos. It has slots for cards (Customise > Cards): the greeting is one. Glass Five columns of wide cards, the dock on a dark band with the focused app's name above it, a light clock with a divider and a greeting, and a soft glow of the app's colour around the dock. The focus is a glass plate that glides from app to app. Down moves the dock up, the clock and buttons step aside, and the name of the focused app shows under its card.

The pictures are the launcher page rendered in a browser with each theme.

items.title: Contributing a theme
items.text:
Themes live in the repository, so a new one is a pull request:

  1. Copy a folder from themes/, for example classic, to themes/<id>/. The id is lower-case letters, digits and -.
  2. Edit theme.json; the rest keeps its default, or the value of the theme named in "extends".
  3. Add preview.jpg: a screenshot of the home screen with your theme (16:9, about 800 px wide, at most 600 KB).
  4. If it uses a wallpaper, add the image to the same folder (.jpg, .png or .webp, at most 1.5 MB, 1920 x 1080) and name it in effects.wallpaper. A typeface goes in the folder too, named in type.fontFile, with its licence file. A wallpaper or typeface must be your own work or under a licence that allows redistribution; say which in the pull request.
  5. Run node tools/theme-index.js to update themes/index.json, then node tools/test.js theme: it checks every theme folder against the schema, that the screenshot is there, and that the index is up to date.
  6. Open the pull request. Once it is merged into main, every TV can download the theme; no release is needed.

When you add a setting to the engine, add one row to SCHEMA in helper/themeschema.js, read its variable in the launcher's CSS (app/src/css/, then node tools/build-pages.js), and run node tools/theme-docs.js to regenerate the table below.

items.title: Making a theme with an AI assistant
items.text:
An assistant such as Claude can write a theme from a description ("a calm blue theme with big tiles and the dock at the bottom"). Give it a checkout of the repository (or these files) and the rules below.

What it needs to read - The table of settings further down this page (or SCHEMA in helper/themeschema.js, the source of that table): every key, its range and its default. - themes/classic/theme.json and one existing theme that is close to the goal, for example themes/bloom/theme.json. - themes/README.md for the folder layout.

Rules - A theme is data only: themes/<id>/theme.json with keys from the table, nothing else. No CSS, no script, no URLs. Unknown keys and out-of-range values are ignored or clamped, so a value that is not in the table has no effect. - Positions and sizes are pixels on a 1920 x 1080 canvas. Keep the clock and the buttons at least 60 px from the screen edges (TVs can crop the picture), and make sure the dock fits: dock.count x dock.w plus the gaps must be at most the screen width (a panel adds dock.panelPad on each side). - Text must stay readable: about 4.5 : 1 between colors.ink and the surfaces it sits on, and a visible focus ring. The text colour on the accent is chosen automatically. - The TV's graphics chip is weak: no blurred or animated wallpapers, one static image at most, 1920 x 1080, at most 1.5 MB (.jpg, .png or .webp), kept in the theme's folder and named in effects.wallpaper. Prefer the dock and grid settings over tricks. - A wallpaper must be original (drawn or generated for the theme) or under a licence that allows redistribution. Do not copy other people's artwork, screenshots or logos, and do not use brand names or trademarks in a theme. - Use "extends" to start from another theme and list only what changes. Do not rename a setting group: name, author, description and extends are the theme's own fields.

Steps 1. Create themes/<id>/theme.json (and the wallpaper, if any). 2. Look at it: node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --out /tmp/preview renders the home screen with made-up apps in headless Chrome and writes rest.png (home), grid.png (the focus moved down into the apps) and menu.png (a menu). It needs Node.js 22 or newer and Chrome. Open the images, fix what looks wrong (overlapping parts, unreadable text, clipped tiles) and render again. 3. When it looks right, node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --write also writes themes/<id>/preview.jpg (needs ffmpeg), the screenshot the TV shows. 4. node tools/theme-index.js updates themes/index.json; node tools/test.js theme checks every theme folder, the screenshot and the index. 5. Commit and open a pull request; say where the wallpaper comes from.

A prompt to start with

Create a theme for CleanYourTV. Read the settings table in docs/themes.md, themes/classic/theme.json and themes/bloom/theme.json. The theme: describe the look and the layout you want. Write themes/<id>/theme.json using only keys from the table (data only; ranges are enforced), generate an original wallpaper if it needs one (1920 x 1080, under 1.5 MB, saved in the theme's folder), render it with node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --out /tmp/preview, look at rest.png, grid.png and menu.png, fix problems and render again, then run node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --write, node tools/theme-index.js and node tools/test.js theme. Keep text readable and the wallpaper my own work.

items.title: Theme files
items.text:
A theme is themes/<id>/theme.json in the repository. Every key is optional. A missing or invalid value keeps the value of the theme named in "extends", or the default, which is the original look, so a theme lists only what it changes. Positions and sizes are in pixels on a 1920 x 1080 canvas.

{
  "name": "Midnight",
  "author": "CleanYourTV",
  "description": "Deep blue with a soft wallpaper and a blue focus.",
  "extends": "classic",
  "colors": { "night": "#060a18", "panel": "#101830", "ink": "#eaf0ff", "accent": "#7aa2ff" },
  "effects": { "glow": 0.8, "wallpaper": "midnight.jpg", "wallpaperDim": 0.25 }
}

items.title: What a theme can set
items.text:
Every part of the home screen has its own position and size, so themes can arrange the screen differently, not only recolour it: the clock, the top buttons (bar), the large app name, the dock and the grid. Each can be anchored to the top or bottom edge and aligned left, centre or right, with an offset. A dock at the bottom turns the grid into an overlay that opens when the focus moves down into it (Back or Up closes it); a dock at the top leaves the grid below it, scrolling.
