items.title: Slots for cards
items.text:
A theme can mark places where cards go: small widgets the user chooses in Customise > Cards (for now the greeting; weather and Home Assistant cards follow). A theme without slots shows no cards and has no Cards row in Customise. Slots are a list in theme.json:

"slots": [
  { "id": "greeting", "anchor": "top", "align": "left", "x": 102, "y": 70, "w": 900, "h": 26, "card": "greeting", "grid": "keep" },
  { "id": "side", "anchor": "top", "align": "right", "x": 96, "y": 170, "w": 520, "h": 520 }
]
Key Values What it does id lower-case letters, digits and - The name of the place. Use greeting (above the clock), clock-side (beside the clock), side (a column on the right) or row (above the dock) where they fit: the card a user chose stays when they switch to another theme with the same slot, and these four have a name in every language. anchor, align, x, y as for the clock Where the slot's box is, counted from that side of the 1920 x 1080 screen; x is not used when centred. w, h px The size of the box. card a card type, for example greeting What the slot shows until the user chooses something else. Without it the slot starts empty. grid keep or hide keep leaves the card on screen while the app grid is open; by default it fades out then.

At most eight slots; values out of range are clamped and a slot with a bad or repeated id is left out. A theme that extends another keeps its slots unless it has its own "slots" (an empty list removes them). In a right-to-left language the slots are mirrored like the rest of the screen.

items.title: Focus, names and motion
items.text:
These settings are off unless a theme sets them, so a theme that does not use them looks as it always did. Glass uses all of them.

  • tile.focus: "glass" replaces the focus ring with a lit glass plate behind the focused tile. It glides from tile to tile (one plate in the dock, one in the grid), with its rim in the focus colour and as wide as tile.ringWidth, tile.ringOffset away from the tile.
  • grid.label: "focus" writes the name of the focused app under its tile in the grid; leave room for it with grid.gapY (about 50 or more), or the name sits over the next row.
  • shelf.motion lets the large name fade or slide when the focus moves; shelf.weight sets how bold it is.
  • grid.header: "fade" moves the clock, the top buttons and the cards out of the way while the focus is in the grid.
  • clock.weight, clock.dateCaps, clock.divider and clock.ampm: "small" change the clock's type. A weight the TV's typeface does not have shows as its nearest weight; a theme with type.fontFile brings its own.
  • effects.glowShape: "center" draws the glow as a large circle around the dock instead of a wash from the top edge.
  • surface.pillGloss gives the top buttons a sheen; colors.dockPanel colours the panel behind the dock (dock.panel is its opacity).

Everything here moves with transform and opacity only, follows effects.speed, stands still while an arrow key is held down, and is mirrored in a right-to-left language.

A theme file holds values only. The service checks every value against the table and clamps numbers to their range; there is no CSS and no script, and a wallpaper is accepted only as a plain file name from the theme's folder that is also a real image of the right type. Anything else is ignored. The launcher draws the wallpaper once and nothing blurs or filters it, because the TV's GPU is weak.

From a shell on the TV:

curl localhost:8765/api/theme/list
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/theme/set -d '{"id":"midnight","accent":"#ff8a3d"}'   # downloads the theme if it is not on the TV
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/theme/revert

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Black screen after switching or rebooting. Wait a minute; if it stays black, restart the TV. If the new Home does not come up, the setup removes the boot scripts and restarts the TV with LG's Home by itself.
  • The Home button opens LG's full-screen Home, not CleanYourTV. Some TVs have a Home Style setting. Set TV Settings > General > Home Settings > Home Style to Basic.
  • Apps do not open, an HDMI input has no picture or the remote no longer controls HDMI-CEC devices (webOS 5 to 23). These followed the restart of the app manager on TVs with LG's native Home (issues 14, 23 and 24). From service 1.6.6 such a TV takes over Home without that restart. Share log shows the steps under Boot steps; open an issue with it if the problem stays.
  • An app is missing from the grid. Check Hidden apps in Customise. Apps without a launch icon are not listed.
  • After a firmware update removed root. Re-root, then run the install command and the setup again.
  • The Input key opens LG's picker. Check the Input key switch in the manager app and run Learn the Input key.
  • A loading circle appears every half minute and the remote stops responding until you hold Back. The Input key can show the Inputs list over the running app with a small app that the service starts in the background. On webOS 6.5 (reports) the TV closes that app again and it keeps the remote. From v1.5.13 webOS before 10 starts the app only when the key is pressed and closes it after use, and on any TV the service switches to that when it had to start the background app three times in ten minutes (picker.mode: ondemand in config.json). Input key > Input key shows chooses by hand; switching the Input key off entirely gives the key back to LG.
  • The manager list does not show Share log or Uninstall. Before v1.5.13 the list could not scroll; update, then move down: the list scrolls and fades where more rows are hidden.
  • Text appears twice in menus or the Live TV list on webOS 5 (blurred, overlapping). webOS 5's browser (Chromium 68) can keep the old text when a list is redrawn. From v1.5.13 the launcher swaps the list for a fresh element there instead of rewriting it.
  • The service restarts by itself. On some TVs Node.js 8 stops with uv_close: Assertion ... failed. From v1.5.13 the service logs its last operations when it finds that the previous run ended without a clean exit; they appear in Share log under the service log, so a report names the cause.
  • FAILED_IPKG_INSTALL. Remove the com.cleanyourtv.manager entry marked half-installed from /media/developer/apps/var/lib/opkg/status and install again.
  • Live TV shows the setup code again. The playlist address was reset or never saved; run the pairing again, or send it with POST /api/live/settings (Live TV).
  • Something is broken after an update. A launcher or service that does not start is replaced by the previous version automatically. Go back to launcher in the manager returns to the previous launcher by hand.
  • Back to LG's Home right now. In the manager, CleanYourTV as Home off, or sh /media/developer/cleanyourtv/undo-home.sh over SSH.

items.title: Reporting a problem
items.text:
An AI assistant can help you read the report and find the cause: see Working on problems with an AI assistant.

Open an issue and attach the output of Share log (manager app, see The manager app). It is masked, so it does not contain your addresses or keys. Say which TV and firmware you have and what you expected.

items.title: What it changes on the TV
items.text:
Only the takeover of Home and the debloat's /etc/hosts lines are applied in RAM at boot, as mounts. Everything else is stored in the writable partitions listed below and stays after a reboot until you uninstall. Nothing under /usr, /etc or the firmware is modified on disk, and a reboot without the boot scripts brings LG's Home back.

The optional voice download (about 80 MB) is stored in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/voice and stays until Remove voice or the uninstall. Optional features contact other services only when you switch them on; see Security.

items.title: At boot
items.text:
1. The Homebrew Channel runs the boot scripts in /var/lib/webosbrew/init.d/.

  2. 10-cleanyourtv-home starts the service and, unless /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE exists, replaces LG's Home. How depends on LG's Home app as it came with the TV (helper/tvprofile.js, homeTakeover; see what differs between webOS versions):

    • LG's Home is a flutter or web app (webOS 24 and newer): a directory holding the launcher is bind-mounted over LG's Home app (/usr/palm/applications/com.webos.app.home). Its appinfo.json is derived from this TV's own stock Home, so nothing of LG's is shipped. The system app manager (sam) is restarted so that it reads the new Home.
    • LG's Home is a native program (webOS 5 to 23): home-standin.sh is bind-mounted over that program (its path comes from the stock Home's appinfo.json, usually /usr/bin/com.webos.app.home) and LG's running Home is stopped once. LG's Home manifest stays in place and the app manager is not restarted: it starts the stand-in whenever Home is launched. The stand-in asks webapp-mgr to open the launcher directory as com.webos.app.home and tries to register with the app manager as Home, so the Home key shows the open launcher again. If the launcher is not open in webapp-mgr within 30 seconds, the stand-in is removed and LG's Home comes back until the next reboot. A file /media/developer/cleanyourtv/home-method holding mount makes such a TV use the first way.

Whenever the app manager is restarted on a TV with LG's native Home or on webOS before 7 (the first way, or the setup registering our extra apps), the services that talk to it (eim, webapp-mgr, preload-manager, memorymanager, those the TV has) are restarted after it (after-sam.sh). Without that, apps stopped opening, an HDMI input lost its picture and HDMI-CEC control stopped (issues 14, 23 and 24). Each step is written to /tmp/cleanyourtv-boot.log, which Share log includes. On webOS 26 (SDK 11) with the flutter or web Home, the same hook restarts arccontroller after the app manager, if it runs: on an OLED65C35LA HDMI ARC to the soundbar stayed silent although the right output was chosen and the controller was running, and restarting that controller brought the sound back (issue 21, found by karim7878). webOS 25 is left alone; eARC keeps working there. 3. About a minute later the debloat runs, if it is on.

Either bind mount lives in RAM. A reboot without the boot scripts, or the Homebrew Channel's failsafe mode, leaves LG's Home as it was.

items.title: Voice (optional)
items.text:
Recognises speech from the remote's microphone on the TV. The text is shown on screen and can be sent to a server you run, to a language model through OpenRouter, or both; the answer is shown as text on screen. Answers are not spoken. No audio is recorded or sent anywhere.

It is off and not installed by default. Nothing described here runs until you install it.

items.title: Installing
items.text:
Voice in the manager app downloads about 80 MB into /media/developer/cleanyourtv/voice. The checksums are pinned in the code; Remove voice deletes everything again.

Part From Speech engine libmoonshine.so and ONNX Runtime the moonshine-voice 0.1.5 package on PyPI (MIT) 64-bit C library ubuntu-base 22.04.5 for arm64 (this TV has a 32-bit userland on a 64-bit kernel, so the 64-bit recogniser brings its own) Model tiny-streaming-en (34 million parameters, int8) download.moonshine.ai (MIT) cytv-asr, a small program that feeds audio to the engine this repository (voice/asr.c, built with voice/build.sh)

items.title: Using it
items.text:
Step How Choose the button Voice > Learn the voice button. Try the remote's microphone button; if the hook does not see it, any spare button works. Then switch Listen on the voice button on. Try without a button Voice > Try it now, or curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/listen Send the text to a server curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"url":"http://server:port/path","token":"optional"}' Pause LG's voice assistant Voice > Switch off LG's voice assistant. It pauses LG's voiceconductor process while voice is on, so LG's own screen and its cloud recognition do not start on the same button. A reboot or turning the switch off undoes it.

On screen a card changes in place while you speak: Listening (moving bars), Recognising or Thinking (dots), then your question in small type above the answer. Reading time follows the length of the answer.

items.title: Sending text to your own server
items.text: The TV sends POST with the JSON body {"text":"...","source":"cleanyourtv","language":"en","time":"..."} and, when a token is set, Authorization: Bearer <token>. If the server answers with JSON ({"title","text","image","seconds"}) or plain text, the answer is shown as a card. The address and token are stored in config.json on the TV only.

items.title: AI chat (OpenRouter)
items.text:
In Voice, Set up from your phone shows a QR code. Scan it with a phone on the same Wi-Fi and enter:

  • your OpenRouter key,
  • a model (the list is read from OpenRouter; any model name can be typed),
  • instructions, and, if you like, the address of your own server.

The page is open for ten minutes or until you save, at a random address. It is plain HTTP, so use it on a network you trust. Model on the TV chooses among the newest models of the main providers, with their price. AI chat (OpenRouter) switches the answers on and off.

The same from a shell:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"llm":{"key":"sk-or-...","model":"openrouter/auto"}}'
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"llm":{"enabled":true}}'

What you say is sent as text to openrouter.ai with the model you chose (a short instruction asks for one to three plain sentences; change it with "system"), and the answer appears on screen. The model remembers the last six exchanges for ten minutes (Forget the conversation clears them). The key is stored in config.json on the TV only. With a server address set as well, the server also receives the text and the model's answer ({"text","answer"}).

You can also ask by text, with the same result, and without the speech download:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/ask -d '{"text":"..."}'

It answers {"text","answer","error"}; add "card":false to skip the screen.

items.title: The speech model
items.text:
Moonshine (Moonshine AI, MIT licence) runs on the TV; there is no cloud recogniser.

Model tiny-streaming-en: about 34 million parameters, encoder and decoder, int8 weights, 45 MB. Runtime ONNX Runtime on the CPU (two ARM cores on the G2). Segmentation The engine's voice-activity detection splits the audio into phrases. The service stops recording after 1.2 s of silence, after 7 s without speech, or after 15 s. Cost on the G2 Load 0.3 s; a 3 s phrase takes about 1.4 s; about 190 MB of memory while recognising, none when idle. Reported accuracy 12.0 % average word error rate on the Open ASR Leaderboard datasets, 4.8 % on LibriSpeech test-clean (figures from the Moonshine project; not measured through the remote's microphone). Language English. Moonshine also publishes German, Spanish, Arabic, Japanese, Mandarin, Tagalog and Vietnamese models and larger English ones (small 123 M, medium 245 M parameters). Audio 16 kHz mono from the microphone stream of LG's voiceinput service. Held in memory while recognising, then discarded; not written to disk or sent anywhere.

The TV's programs are 32-bit ARM on a 64-bit kernel and the recogniser is a 64-bit program, so cytv-asr runs through the 64-bit loader and libraries that the download places in the same folder. Nothing in the system folders is changed.

Only text goes further: to your server, to OpenRouter, or nowhere. LG's own assistant is a separate path with its own cloud recognition; Switch off LG's voice assistant pauses it while voice is on.

items.title: Home Assistant (Assist)
items.text:
The recognised text can go to Home Assistant's Assist (POST /api/conversation/process), which turns on lights, answers questions about your home and so on. Its answer is shown as text on the card. Answers are not spoken.

In Voice, Set up from your phone also asks for:

  • the address of Home Assistant, for example http://homeassistant.local:8123,
  • a long-lived access token (your Home Assistant profile page, under Security),
  • whether to accept a self-signed certificate (only matters for https:// addresses),
  • which answers first.

Choosing Home Assistant (Assist) in the menu tests the connection and shows the name and version of your Home Assistant.

Setting Behaviour Home Assistant first, then the AI (default) The text goes to Assist. If Assist understood it, its answer is shown. If it did not (no_intent_match), or Home Assistant cannot be reached, the same text goes to the AI chat, when that is switched on. Without the AI, Assist's own message is shown. Home Assistant only The AI is never asked. The AI only Home Assistant is not asked.

Assist agent lists the conversation agents of your Home Assistant (its conversation.* entities) and lets you choose one; the default is the built-in agent. A conversation id is passed on, so follow-up questions keep their context; a new conversation starts after ten quiet minutes or after Forget the conversation.

The same from a shell:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"ha":{"url":"http://homeassistant.local:8123","token":"eyJ..."}}'
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"ha":{"route":"ha-only","agent":"conversation.home_assistant","selfSigned":false}}'
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/ha-test
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/ask -d '{"text":"turn on the living room light"}'

route is ha-first, ha-only or ai-only; {"ha":{"clear":true}} removes the address and the token. /api/voice/ask answers {"text","answer","via","error"}, where via is ha or ai.

The token is stored in config.json on the TV only and is never returned by the service. Only the recognised text goes to your Home Assistant. With a plain http:// address the token is visible on your network.

items.title: Wallpapers
items.text: Your own photos behind the home screen, from two sources: photos you upload from a phone, and photos from albums on your Immich server. Both end up in one library on the TV.

items.title: Switching it on
items.text:
In the launcher, Customise > Wallpapers:

Row What it does Use Wallpapers On: a photo from the library replaces the theme's background, in every theme. Off: the theme as it is. New photo When the photo changes: each time Home opens, or also every 10 or 30 seconds, every minute, or every 3, 5, 15 or 60 minutes while Home is on screen. The photos cross-fade. Photo All photos, shuffled (a new one as set above), or One chosen photo, which stays. Choosing it here goes back to all photos. Choose a photo... Browse the photos on the screen, one at a time and whole: Left and Right to browse, OK to use the one on the screen as your wallpaper, Back to leave. With the Magic Remote, the left and right thirds of the screen browse and the middle chooses. Add photos... Opens the manager app on its Wallpapers screen.

The photo is chosen at random and darkened like a theme's wallpaper (the theme's own darkening, or 40 % when it has none). With no photos in the library, Home looks as before. The theme Still switches the cross-fade off along with the other animations.

items.title: Adding photos
items.text:
The photos of a photo feed (for example the family calendar's) are Wallpapers photos too, as soon as the feed is set up: nothing to add here. They are fetched one at a time when shown and do not count towards the 150 MB below.

In the manager app, Wallpapers > Manage from your phone shows a QR code and a 6-digit code. Scan it with a phone on the same Wi-Fi. The page has two parts:

  • Upload photos: choose one or more photos. Each one is scaled on the phone before it is sent (to 3840 or 1920 pixels on the long side, see Picture size), which also turns an iPhone's HEIC photos into JPEG. The page shows the progress and what failed. Uploaded photos are listed below, each with a × to delete it.
  • Configure Immich: the server address and an API key, then Test connection and save. Choose albums and Save albums and sync (choosing albums while a sync runs starts another one right after it). The synced photos are listed; tap one to hide it from the TV (tap again to show it).

The page is served by the TV itself on port 8791, needs the code shown on the TV, stays open while you use it (at most an hour) and closes when you leave the QR screen. It is not encrypted: photos and the Immich key travel over your Wi-Fi.

items.title: The manager screen
items.text: Row What it does Manage from your phone The QR code for the phone page. Local uploads, Immich, Total How many photos there are per source, when Immich was last synced and its last error, and the space used. Sync now Downloads new and changed photos from the chosen Immich albums and removes the ones that left them. Picture size 4K (3840 pixels, the default) or Full HD (1920). Applies to new uploads and to the next Immich sync. On a 4K TV, Home is laid out at 1920 x 1080 but drawn at 3840 x 2160, so a 4K photo is shown pixel for pixel; Full HD fits about four times as many photos in 150 MB. Remove all uploads Deletes every uploaded photo, after a confirmation. Disconnect Immich Forgets the address and the key and deletes the Immich photos, after a confirmation.

items.title: Immich
items.text:
Create an API key in Immich under Account settings > API keys with at least the album.read, asset.read and asset.view permissions (asset.download too for full-size pictures on older servers). The key is kept in the service's settings file (config.json, readable by root only); the TV's pages only ever see its last four characters, and it is not logged.

A sync reads the chosen albums (your own and the ones shared with you) through the Immich API (on Immich 2 and newer, where an album no longer lists its photos, by searching for the album's photos), skips videos and photos in the trash, and downloads each photo once, newest first. A photo is downloaded again only when Immich reports a different checksum; it is tracked by its Immich ID, not its file name. Photos that are no longer in a chosen album are deleted from the TV; nothing else is touched. At 4K the TV asks for Immich's full-size picture (Immich 1.120 or newer), then the original when it is a JPEG, PNG or WebP, then the preview; at Full HD it uses the preview (about 1440 pixels).

The sync runs every six hours, and with Sync now. Shortly after the TV starts it only runs when the last sync is more than a day old. When Immich cannot be reached the photos already on the TV stay, and the error is shown. Showing a photo never needs Immich.

items.title: Limits and storage
items.text:
Uploads At most 100 photos, 12 MB each; JPEG, PNG and WebP (checked by their content, not their name). Immich At most 300 photos. Space 150 MB for both together. A full library refuses uploads and stops the sync with a message.

The photos are stored in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/wallpapers/: upload/ (each under a random name), immich/ (each under its Immich ID) and index.json, which records the source, size and checksum of every file. Only files listed there are ever deleted. They survive restarts and updates; Uninstall removes them with the rest.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: The code is on GitHub, a fork of lasharor/cleanyourtv-WebOS (About this fork). Issues and pull requests are welcome, especially reports from TVs that are not in the tested list.

items.title: Layout
items.text: Folder or file What it is app/ The launcher: src/ (its CSS and script files), the built index.html and version.json. manager/, picker/, notify/ The three apps of the package (manager, Inputs picker, picture notification card); the manager is built from manager/src. themes/ The themes: one folder each (theme.json, preview.jpg, a wallpaper) and index.json. Read by the TVs from GitHub, not shipped with the service; contribute one. helper/ The root service (Node.js), one module per part: see Internals. scripts/ Boot, setup and restore scripts: bootstrap.sh, 10-cleanyourtv-home, stage-home.sh, undo-home.sh, the debloat scripts. voice/ Source of the small speech program cytv-asr and its build script. third-party/ The bundled inputhook files and the QR library. tools/ check.sh: every check (the tests in tools/test under Node 8.12.0 and the current Node, the built pages); build-pages.js: builds the launcher and manager pages from their sources; theme-docs.js: regenerates the table of theme settings in the docs; theme-index.js: writes themes/index.json; theme-preview.mjs: renders a theme in headless Chrome (and makes its screenshot). ipk/build.py Builds the release files. package.json, tsconfig.json, eslint.config.js, .prettierrc.json Development tools only: type checks, lint and formatting. compat.json The list of tested firmware the setup reads. install.sh, uninstall.sh The installer and uninstaller. docs/, zensical.toml This documentation.

items.title: Building
items.text:
python3 ipk/build.py

writes the release files to dist/: com.cleanyourtv.manager_<version>_all.ipk, frontend-<version>.tgz and a .sha256 file for each, and the Homebrew Channel repository: apps.json and com.cleanyourtv.manager.manifest.json, which point at the package in the release tagged v<version> (CYTV_TAG and CYTV_REPO change the tag and the repository). The Homebrew Channel reads releases/latest/download/apps.json, so the newest release is what it offers. The service version is VERSION in helper/helper.js; the launcher version is app/version.json and VERSION in app/src/js/core.js (the build refuses to run when they differ). Run node tools/build-pages.js after changing a page's sources.

items.title: Translations
items.text: The screens are written in English and translated from i18n/<language>.json (English text as the key); tools/build-pages.js puts what each page uses into it, and node tools/i18n.js shows how complete each language is. See i18n/README.md for adding a language or a text.

items.title: Branches and releases
items.text:
Branch What it is dev Where all work lands, including pull requests (it is the default branch). Every push publishes the dev build. main The last release. Only the release workflow moves it. any other Your own work in progress. Pushes run the checks but publish nothing; merge into dev to let people try it.

The release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) runs when it is started by hand (Actions > Release > Run workflow); this fork has no daily schedule, so nothing is released without a person deciding it. When the files that go into the package changed on dev since the last release, tools/release.sh raises the patch version of the service (and of the launcher when app/ changed), commits that to dev and moves main to it; the workflow then builds and publishes v<version> with the commit subjects as release notes. Raise a minor or major version by hand on dev and the script keeps it. CYTV_DRY=1 sh tools/release.sh shows what the next release would contain.

Using an AI assistant to find or fix a bug is welcome: see Working on problems with an AI assistant and AGENTS.md in the repository root.

items.title: Rules of the road
items.text:
• Per-TV differences go in helper/tvprofile.js, with a case in tools/test/tvprofile.test.js; settings are changed only through config.update (helper/config.js).
  • Support webOS 5. The service must run on Node.js 8: no crypto.randomInt, no fs.promises, no URL as a global, no mkdirSync({recursive}), no http.get(url, options). Use helper/netcompat.js. sh tools/check.sh catches regressions.
  • The pages run in Chromium 68 and newer. The launcher is written in ES5 without a framework, and only transform and opacity are animated, because the TV's GPU is weak. No flex gap (Chromium before 84 ignores it): space flex children with sibling margins.
  • Do not store private data in the repository. No playlist addresses, access keys, IP addresses or names.
  • Documentation must match the code. When a feature changes, change its page here and, if it is mentioned there, the README.
  • Licence. The project is MIT. Do not copy code from GPL projects into it; describe behaviour and write your own.

items.title: Adding a TV to the tested list
items.text: Open an issue with the output of Share log and say whether it worked. A pull request that adds an entry to compat.json is welcome too: firmware, optionally sdk, homeType, status and a note.

items.title: Dev builds
items.text: Every push to dev publishes the dev build that people can install from the manager app. See Testing and CI.

items.title: The pieces
items.text: Piece Runs as Notes The service (helper.js and modules) Node.js, root, started by the boot script Listens on 127.0.0.1:8765; bridges the web pages to luna-send (LG's service bus), serves app icons, runs Live TV, notifications, voice, the manager API and the input hook. The launcher (app/index.html) A web app in LG's web runtime, mounted as LG's Home Reads apps and settings from the service. Manager, picker, notify Web apps installed from the package The picker and notify apps are hidden; the service starts them. The input hook Injected into LG's input processes Runs a command when a bound remote key is pressed.

items.title: The service
items.text:
helper/helper.js only wires the parts together. Each part is a module with create(ctx) that returns its name, the paths it answers (paths or a prefix), handle(req, res, path, body) and an optional start(). A part that fails to load is left out and listed at GET /api/service; the others keep working.

Module What it is paths.js Every place on the TV the service reads or writes; the tests move them with environment variables. config.js The settings in config.json. config.update(source, fn) reads, changes and writes in one step, so two parts never overwrite each other's settings; every change of an option, a learned key or the Input-key mode is logged with its source (config: options.inputKey true -> false (manager)), which shows up in Share log. tvprofile.js Everything that differs between TVs: the Input key's default mode, the notification window type, whether the firmware is in compat.json, whether LG's Home is a supported kind, how Home is taken over (homeTakeover) and which services are restarted after the app manager (afterSam). The service saves it in tv.json (GET /api/tv); the setup script asks the same rules (node tvprofile.js get notifyWindow --sdk 10.2.2). exec.js, luna.js, fetch.js The one way to start a program (time limits without Node's own timeout option, which can abort Node 8), to call luna-send, and to download (redirects, gzip, size and time limits, dropped connections). server.js, web.js The HTTP server with the origin rules, and small reply helpers. apps.js, running.js The app list, icons, usage, launching and the launcher's own settings; the running apps to close (Back on Home). inputkey.js, inputhook.js, picker.js The Input key: the hook in LG's input processes, the key binds, the Inputs picker. manager.js, updates.js, debloat.js The manager's API, updates from GitHub releases with rollback, switching the debloat. live.js, notify.js, notifyapi.js One feature each. wallpapers.js Wallpapers: the photo library (uploads and Immich, apart on disk, with an index), the phone page on port 8791 and the Immich sync. theme.js, themeschema.js Themes: themeschema.js holds every setting a theme can make, the checks and how a theme becomes CSS variables; theme.js reads themes from GitHub and keeps them on the TV. voice.js, answers.js Voice: the microphone, the recogniser, the phone setup page; answers.js asks Home Assistant, a language model or your server. selfupdate.js, sharelog.js Programs the manager runs when the service is not running.

items.title: The pages
items.text: The launcher and the manager are built from source files: app/src and manager/src hold index.html with @include lines and the CSS and script files they name. node tools/build-pages.js writes app/index.html and manager/app/index.html, the single files the TV loads; the built files are committed, so an update and the theme preview read them as before. The picker and the notification card are small and stay single files.

items.title: How the launcher becomes Home
items.text:
1. 10-cleanyourtv-home runs at boot and starts the service.
  2. stage-home.sh builds a directory holding the launcher plus an appinfo.json derived from this TV's own stock Home (saved in backup/home-appinfo.orig.json the first time), switched to the web type.
  3. tvprofile.js decides the way from the stock Home's kind (homeTakeover):
    • mount (flutter or web Home, webOS 24 and newer): the script bind-mounts that directory over /usr/palm/applications/com.webos.app.home, restarts the system app manager (sam) so it reads the new Home, and launches Home again. On webOS before 7 and with a native Home, after-sam.sh then restarts the services that keep talking to the old app manager (afterSam).
    • standin (native Home, webOS 5 to 23): jtool.js exe finds LG's Home program in the stock appinfo.json and the script bind-mounts home-standin.sh over it, then stops LG's running Home once. sam is not restarted and keeps LG's Home manifest, so it starts the stand-in for Home. The stand-in sends wam-launch.json (written by stage-home.sh with jtool.js wamlaunch) to com.palm.webappmanager/launchApp, which opens the directory from step 2 as com.webos.app.home, and holds a registration with sam so the Home key sends it relaunch. Without registration, sam restarts the stand-in on the Home key, which opens the launcher the same way. /tmp/cleanyourtv-home-standin holds the program's path while it is mounted; reload-home.sh, undo-home.sh, the debloat hook and the manager's status read it. If webapp-mgr does not list the launcher within 30 seconds, undo-home.sh temp brings LG's Home back. home-method holding mount forces the first way.
  4. A watchdog keeps checking that the service answers. If it stays unreachable for about a minute, it restores LG's Home until the next reboot.

Nothing is written under /usr: the mount disappears at reboot. DISABLE in /media/developer/cleanyourtv makes the script skip it.

items.title: Updates and rollback
items.text:
• Launcher. The manager downloads frontend-<version>.tgz and its .sha256, checks the list of files in the archive (only app/...), unpacks, checks version.json, swaps it in (the old one becomes app.prev), reloads Home and waits up to 40 seconds for the new launcher to report that it started. If it does not, the previous launcher is swapped back.
  • Service. The manager downloads the package, installs it with the system's app installer and runs bootstrap.sh update, which keeps the running files in backup/service-prev.tgz, copies the new ones, restarts the service and waits for it to answer with the new version. If it does not, the previous files are restored.
  • Dev builds. Same flows, from the pre-release dev; the commit in a BUILD file is how two builds with one version number are told apart.

items.title: Older webOS versions
items.text:
webOS 5 and 6 ship Node.js 8, and webOS 6 has Chromium 79.

  • helper/netcompat.js supplies URL, URLSearchParams, crypto.randomInt, mkdir -p and the http(s).get(url, options) form.
  • What differs between versions is decided in helper/tvprofile.js: the picker is started on demand and the notification window is an overlay before webOS 25 (SDK 10); LG's native Home (webOS 5 to 23) is taken over by the stand-in, without restarting the app manager. The table is in Tested TVs.
  • The pages do not use flex gap, which Chromium before 84 ignores: spacing between flex children is a sibling margin (.row > * + * { margin-left: 22px; }). Grid gap is fine from Chromium 66. The focus ring of a tile is a ::before with its own radius, because Chromium before 94 draws an outline as a rectangle.
  • The service accepts the file://<appId>-webos origin that webOS 6 apps send, for our own apps and the Home slot only.
  • scripts/reload-home.sh restarts webapp-mgr on webOS 6, where a relaunch alone keeps the old page.

Checked by reports, not by the maintainer

The maintainer's TV runs webOS 25. webOS 5, 6 and 23 are known from reports (Tested TVs). Every change is checked under Node 8.12.0 and in Chromium 68 and 79 (sh tools/check.sh --chromium), not on a TV of those versions.

items.title: Things that were tried
items.text:
A native launcher

A launcher written in C with SDL2 (so it draws on the GPU without the web runtime) was built and run as LG's Home on a webOS 25 TV. It worked, started quickly and used about as much memory and CPU as the web launcher, but LG's compositor shows "Do you want to exit the app?" when Back is pressed in a native app, and setting a key mask on the window did not stop it. It is kept on the native-launcher branch for reference and is not part of the project.

items.title: All checks in one command
items.text:
sh tools/check.sh

runs everything a push or a release needs:

  1. the tests in tools/test under Node.js 8.12.0, the version webOS 5 and 6 ship (downloaded once from nodejs.org, checksum verified, cached in ~/.cache/cleanyourtv);
  2. the same tests under the Node.js of your computer, when it is another version;
  3. a check that the launcher and the manager pages are built from their sources (node tools/build-pages.js --check).

With --chromium it also runs the launcher, the manager and the Inputs picker in Chromium 68 and 79, the browser engines of webOS 5 and 6 (tools/oldchrome.js, headless, against a stand-in service): a page that throws a script error there or does not draw its tiles, rows or inputs fails the check. The engines are Chromium snapshots from Google's storage, checked against pinned SHA-256 sums (about 100 MB each, downloaded once). CYTV_SHOTS=<folder> keeps a screenshot of every page per engine; CI keeps them as an artifact of each run.

Nothing leaves your machine apart from the downloads. One area of tests on its own: node tools/test.js live (the names are the files in tools/test without .test.js), or node tools/test/live.test.js.

items.title: Types, lint and formatting
items.text:
package.json lists the development tools: TypeScript, ESLint and Prettier. None of them is shipped; the service and the pages have no dependencies. After npm install once, tools/check.sh (or node tools/lint.js) also runs:

  • TypeScript on the service (helper/*.js), from the code and its JSDoc comments, without compiling anything (tsconfig.json). It found a missing http import in the voice setup page that no test had reached.
  • ESLint on the service, the scripts and the tools, and on the script of every page the TV loads, as ES5 with the TV's globals (eslint.config.js): a name that is used but never defined, a variable declared twice, unreachable code.
  • Prettier in check mode. npm run format formats the code and rebuilds the pages.

items.title: The tests
items.text:
Each file in tools/test is a small program that prints one line per check (ok or FAIL) and runs in a fresh process with its own temporary folder; helper/paths.js points the service's folders there. Local servers stand in for GitHub, playlists, Home Assistant and the TV's own services.

File What it checks api.test.js Starts the real service (helper/helper.js) with a stand-in for luna-send and calls every route of the service API. The replies must equal tools/test/golden/api.json, recorded from version 1.5.16: a change inside the service cannot change what the launcher, the manager and the scripts see. Record again (--record) only when a change of the API is intended. service.test.js Every service file parses and loads; nothing needs a Node newer than 8.12 (optional chaining, fs.rmSync, the timeout option of an asynchronous child process, ...); TV paths only in paths.js. pages.test.js The page scripts are ES5 (parsed with a vendored copy of acorn), nothing in the pages is newer than Chromium 68, and the built pages match their sources. tvprofile.test.js The per-TV decisions for webOS 5, 6.5, 25 and 26 and an unknown TV, from the service and from the shell. scripts.test.js The shell scripts parse; an update keeps the options the user chose; the setup asks tvprofile.js; the debloat's /etc/hosts fallback. manager.test.js Options, keys and the Input-key modes in the manager API; the settings store and its change log. updates.test.js Update checks against a stand-in for the GitHub API: stable and test channels, builds of one version, a dropped connection. fetch.test.js, netcompat.test.js, diag.test.js The HTTP client (redirects, gzip, limits, dropped connections, time limits), the Node 8 compatibility layer, starting programs. live.test.js, theme.test.js, voice.test.js, notifyapi.test.js, picker.test.js One feature each.

A fix needs a test that fails without it, whenever the bug can be reproduced without a TV.

items.title: Pages
items.text:
The built pages are plain HTML files, so they can be opened in a desktop Chrome with a small mock of the service on 127.0.0.1:8765 and driven with scripted key events (tools/theme-preview.mjs does this for the home screen). That is how the launcher, Live TV and manager screens are checked before they go to a TV. The mock needs to answer /api/apps, /api/live/* and /api/manager/* with the shapes in Service API.

What cannot be checked on a computer

Playback of real streams, the TV's remote and pointer, the on-screen keyboard and anything that depends on LG's compositor need a TV.

items.title: Timings on a TV
items.text:
The launcher, the Inputs picker, the Input key and Live TV write short perf lines to the service log: how long the launcher takes to draw (from the saved layout, and with the service's answer), how long from the Input key to the picker on screen, and how long from choosing a channel to moving picture. After using the TV for a while,

sh tools/perf-tv.sh <tv-ip>

prints them (read-only, over SSH). tools/oldchrome.js prints the launcher's time in Chromium 68 and 79 on your computer, which is only a rough comparison: a TV is slower.

items.title: Continuous integration
items.text:
Workflow When What dev-build.yml Every push to dev, and after each release Runs tools/check.sh --chromium, builds the package with the commit in a BUILD file and publishes it as the pre-release dev release.yml By hand (no schedule in this fork) When the package changed since the last release: checks, raises the version (tools/release.sh), moves main to dev, publishes v<version> checks.yml Pull requests and pushes to any branch but dev Runs tools/check.sh --chromium and builds the package docs.yml Pushes that touch the documentation, and after a release that changed it Builds this site; deploys it to GitHub Pages from main

The dev build appears in the manager app's Update channel list; see Dev builds.
